study.title: 1 Corinthians 6 - Disputes among brethren, holiness of body and belonging to Christ
study.overview: Paul corrects three problems connected with each other: the willingness of Christians to bring disputes against each other before unbelieving judges; the remembrance that sinful practices exclude from the Kingdom of God; and the need to live with the body in holiness. The chapter unites community discipline, real conversion and sexual purity, showing that Christian freedom is not a license to sin, because the believer belongs to Christ and was bought for high price.

outline.title: Disputes between brothers and spiritual shame
outline.explanation: Paul reproves brothers who come into court before the unjust rather than resolve the controversies within the community. The argument is that if the saints will participate in the judgment of the world and even the angels, they should be able to deal with small issues with wisdom, peace and humility. Instead, there is moral defeat: brothers harm brothers.

outline.title: The contrast between old life and the new identity
outline.explanation: The apostle recalls that certain practices incompatible with the Kingdom of God are not irrelevant nor can they be treated lightly. He enumerates serious sins and then highlights grace: some of them were so, but they were washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of God.

outline.title: Christian Freedom and the Purpose of the Body
outline.explanation: Paul corrects the idea that everything that is allowed is necessarily useful. The body does not exist for sexual sin, but for the Lord, and the resurrection of Christ guarantees ours. As the bodies of believers are members of Christ, uniting them with sexual sin is a profound spiritual contradiction.

outline.title: Flee from sexual sin and glorify God
outline.explanation: The order is practical and urgent: to flee from sexual sin. Paul teaches that this sin reaches its own body in a special way, because the body of the believer is the temple of the Holy Spirit and no longer belongs to himself. The final basis is redemption: believers have been bought for high price and must glorify God with body and spirit.

study.context: The notes show that the church in Corinth was marked by divisions and lack of practical wisdom to resolve internal conflicts. There was also tolerance for serious sins and a misuse of Christian freedom. In this context, Paul applies the gospel to community life and to the use of the body, without treating faith as something only inland or just spiritual.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that the church already participates, in anticipation, of the authority of God's people in the future judgment; therefore, it must reflect today the wisdom of the Kingdom. He also states that true conversion involves a break with sin and new identity in Christ: being washed, sanctified, and justified. Moreover, the body of the believer has real spiritual value: he is destined to the Lord, indwelling of the Holy Spirit and an instrument for the glory of God. Redemption is not just forgiveness; it is lordship of Christ over the whole person. Christian freedom, therefore, is always limited by love, spiritual utility and fidelity to God.

scholarViews.insight: Christians should not resolve serious differences through secular courts, but with the help of other believers; this is based on the future vocation to judge the world.
Paul teaches that the wicked will not inherit the Kingdom of God, remembering that reigning sins exclude entry into the Kingdom and that the old life of the Corinthians was really abandoned by grace.
Believers were bought with the blood of Christ, and therefore do not belong to themselves; they must use body, soul and spirit to serve and honor God.

questions: What conflicts between brothers do I try to solve in a carnal way, rather than seeking Christian wisdom, peace and humility?
Is there any area of my life in which I treat freedom as an excuse, and not as a call to discipline and spiritual utility?
How can I honor God with my body today, especially in thoughts, habits, and purity?
study.practice: This week, choose a concrete attitude: if there is a tension with another Christian, seek first direct and humble reconciliation, before expanding the conflict. Also review an area of personal freedom and ask if it really builds. In the field of purity, establish clear limits and ask God to flee from what feeds sexual sin. Remember daily: your body does not belong to you in an absolute sense; it was bought by Christ for the glory of God.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not detail all the terms on the list of sins nor do they broadly develop the expression about judging the world and the angels; therefore, the explanation follows only what is explicitly supported in the comments given. Historical or linguistic data that does not appear in the notes have not been used either.
